page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96 is a compute-focused server instance featuring 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing dedicated CPU allocation with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 360 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage for persistent data.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. In benchmark evaluations, the c4-standard-96 demonstrates strong multi-core performance, achieving top-tier status in Geekbench multi-core testing, image processing, and text processing. It also excels in cryptographic tasks, with Passmark CPU encryption scoring in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, registering strong read and write speeds for both cached and uncached blocks.

While single-core performance and text generation for large language models fall into the average tier, the instance delivers exceptional throughput for static web serving and prompt processing. The lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, making it less suitable for heavy local database caching or GPU-accelerated deep learning. However, its high resource density and strong multi-threaded capabilities make it highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads such as software compilation, ray tracing, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM prompt processing.
